scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports. Known source-confirmed gaps only, not an exhaustive acceptance claim.

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: Go's `pkg/sessiontxn` has no Rust package. Go routes every transaction decision through one `TxnContextProvider` per transaction (`isolation.OptimisticTxnContextProvider`, `PessimisticRRTxnContextProvider`, `PessimisticRCTxnContextProvider`, `PessimisticSerializableTxnContextProvider`, `staleread.StalenessTxnContextProvider`), chosen by `EnterNewTxn` and driven by `OnStmtStart` / `OnStmtErrorForNextAction` / `OnStmtRetry` / `AdviseWarmup` / `AdviseOptimizeWithPlan` / `GetStmtReadTS` / `GetStmtForUpdateTS`. The port has no provider type: the same decisions are made in place in `tidb-session` (`txn_manager.rs`, `txn.rs`'s staleness arm, `dispatch.rs`'s RC check-ts and after-query-error arms), `tidb-sessionctx` (`PessimisticTxnProvider`, a two-variant enum the planner reads), `tidb-store-driver-txn` (`cluster_table_storage.rs`'s `OnPessimisticStmtStart` and RC `getStmtTS`) and `tidb-domain-core` (`cluster_transactions.rs`'s `ActivateTxn` wait and `OnStmtRetry`). Each new isolation rule has to be found and repeated at every site, where Go adds one provider method.

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: The parser builds `EXPLAIN` in a different order from Go. Go's `parseExplainStmt` looks at the token after EXPLAIN [ANALYZE] [FORMAT] and only parses SELECT, INSERT, REPLACE, UPDATE, DELETE, ALTER, WITH, TABLE, VALUES, IMPORT or `(`; any other token is a syntax error at that token. `parse_explain_tail` parses any statement first and then rejects what is not a query, a DML or ALTER TABLE. Two visible effects: (1) `EXPLAIN LOAD DATA ...` (also CALL and BATCH, which are `DmlStmt` here) parses and fails at execution with 1105 `EXPLAIN of LoadData is not supported yet`, where Go answers 1064; (2) the 1064 for `EXPLAIN SHOW TABLES`, `EXPLAIN SET @a = 1`, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE SHOW TABLES` and `EXPLAIN FORMAT='plan_tree' ANALYZE SELECT ...` points at the end of the text (`column 19 near ""`) where Go points at the inner statement (`column 12 near "SHOW TABLES"`). `ADMIN SHOW TELEMETRY` has the same position difference (Go `column 5`, Rust `column 20`). The parser ring (`difftests/INTEGRATION_PARSER_DIFF.md`) compares acceptance and restore only, so it does not see error positions. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: A window frame bound takes any expression here. Go's `parseFrameBound` accepts only a number literal, a `?` marker or `INTERVAL expr unit`, as the yacc grammar did, and answers 1064 for `ROWS BETWEEN 1+0 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`; this port parses `parse_expr(PREDICATE + 1)` and runs the query (4 rows). The planner's non-constant-bound refusal (`window.rs`, `evalAstExprWithPlanCtx ... is not ported`) exists only because the parser lets such bounds through. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

The `tidb-server` binary does not take Go's command line. `parse_node_config` first lets `main_flags.rs` take the flags it ports from `initFlagSet`, then parses its own options, which accept only the `--name` form: Go's `-store unistore -path ...` is refused with `unsupported option -store`. It adds options Go has no counterpart for (`--auth-file`, `--load-privileges`, `--lease-ms`, `--affinity-cpus`, `--max-connections`, `--connection-timeout-ms`, `--max-allowed-packet`, `--no-auto-tls`, `--no-disconnect-on-expired-password`, `--ssl-*`, `--cluster-ssl-*`). One of them picks a second account source: `--auth-file` reads users from a TSV file (`ConfiguredUserStore::load`) and refuses a non-loopback listener, and a unistore node started without it fails with `missing required option --auth-file` unless `--load-privileges` is given. Go has one flag set and one account source, `mysql.user` loaded by the privilege cache.

`Uptime` (SHOW STATUS and COM_STATISTICS) counts from the first time it is read, not from process start, on a node started with `--load-privileges`. `server_start_unix_timestamp` is a lazy `OnceLock` that only `configured_account_store` (the `--auth-file` path) touches during startup; observed: a node up for 25 minutes answered `Uptime 0`, then 15, 21. Go reads `infosync` `ServerInfo.StartTimestamp`, set when the server info is created at startup. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

GRANT and REVOKE with an object type are refused. `GRANT SELECT ON TABLE sa.t TO u` and its REVOKE answer 1105 `GRANT ... ON FUNCTION/PROCEDURE is not supported yet` because `grant_stmt` refuses any `object_type`, including `Table`; Go ignores the object type and grants at table level. For FUNCTION / PROCEDURE Go answers 1144 (`Illegal GRANT/REVOKE command`). A column list at database scope (`GRANT SELECT (b) ON sa.* ...`) answers 1105 `GRANT/REVOKE with a column list is not supported yet` where Go answers 1146 `Table 'sa.' doesn't exist`. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

LDAP authentication is not ported. Accounts with `authentication_ldap_simple` / `authentication_ldap_sasl` can be created, the connection switches to the cleartext / SASL client plugin, and the `authentication_ldap_*` variables exist, but the verifier always answers access denied (`configured_user_store.rs`: "this server has neither configured"). Go binds to the LDAP server through `ldap.LDAPSimpleAuthImpl.AuthLDAPSimple` / `LDAPSASLAuthImpl.AuthLDAPSASL`, configured by those variables' `SetGlobal` hooks.

A query that parses to no statement (only a comment) answers an OK packet with 0 affected rows and no message. Go's `handleQuery` calls `writeOK`, which reports the session's current affected rows, last insert ID and message, so after `INSERT ... VALUES (..),(..),(..)` a comment-only query answers `3 rows affected, Records: 3 Duplicates: 0` and after a REPLACE `1 row affected`. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

`SHOW SESSION_STATES` encodes a different set of session variables from Go's. On a fresh session Go's `sys-vars` include `character_set_server` and not `tidb_opt_tiflash_concurrency_factor`; this port's are the reverse (other keys equal). Go keeps a variable only when `GetSessionStatesSystemVar` finds it in the session's `systems` cache, so the difference is in which variables a new session caches. A session migrated between a Go and a Rust node (TiProxy) can lose or gain a value. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

`FOREIGN KEY ... MATCH PARTIAL` is refused with 1105 `MATCH PARTIAL is not supported yet`. Go creates the table and warns 1064 `The MATCH clause is parsed but ignored by any storage engine`, as both already do for MATCH FULL. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

Materialized views are ported up to their statements (phases in `rust/docs/go-shape-refactors-execplan.md`): `TableInfo` keeps Go master's `materialized_view*` fields byte for byte, the base table's DML writes its MV log rows as Go's does, the action types, schema diffs and `tidb_mview_*` / `tidb_mlog_*` variables are Go master's, and the parser takes every materialized view statement (CREATE / ALTER / DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW [LOG], REFRESH, PURGE, CANCEL, COMPARE, the SHOW forms) with Go master's restore text and syntax errors. `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG`, `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG` and `ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG` (PURGE and ADD COLUMN) run as Go master's do, DROP / TRUNCATE / RENAME TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE / DROP / ALTER INDEX, PARTITION BY, REMOVE PARTITIONING and EXCHANGE PARTITION refuse a log and its base table as Go master's do, MODIFY / CHANGE COLUMN of a logged base table retypes the log's tracked column as Go master's does (a base table with dependent materialized views is refused until those are ported), (the log table Go builds, the base table's `MaterializedViewBase`, the `mysql.tidb_mlog_purge_info` row with its schedule, Go's refusals and the `tidb_mview_enable` gate); on a base table that is itself a materialized view the DDL session holds the view's refresh advisory lock for the job's delivery, as Go master's does. CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW runs as Go master's does: the planner's SELECT build and column count, `validateCreateMaterializedViewQuery` (via `tidb-mviewutil`), the view table from the SELECT's output types with its group key and `MaterializedViewInfo`, the owner's create step and its initial build, the refresh and refresh-source rows, and the rollback of a failed build. ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW (COMMENT, REFRESH with its schedule row, ATTRIBUTES) and DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW run as Go master's do too. The build runs Go's INSERT path (`REPLACE INTO view <definition>`); Go's TiKV store builds by IMPORT INTO instead, which this node does not run for it. `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW ... COMPLETE IN PLACE` runs as Go master's does (advisory lock, refresh-info row lock, history rows, DELETE + INSERT of the definition, refresh-source baseline, success persist, failure alert), and so does COMPLETE OUT OF PLACE (shadow table, build, cutover DDL, shadow cleanup), except Go's `ensureMVRefreshSchemaVersion` reload guard and the TiKV store's IMPORT INTO build (this port builds by INSERT). The other REFRESH modes (DELTA APPLY, FAST), DRY RUN / PROFILE, PURGE / CANCEL / COMPARE and the SHOW forms are refused as unsupported statements. This branch's bootstrap does not create Go master's five materialized view tables (`mysql.tidb_mview_refresh_info` .. `tidb_mlog_purge_hist`, Go master's `upgradeToVer316`). The mview background service (`pkg/mvservice`) and its schedule, the planner's FAST-refresh delta plan (`pkg/planner/mview`) and the executor's delta merge aggregation are absent. IMPORT INTO depends on them in one place: a next-gen IMPORT INTO ... FROM SELECT runs on a DXF worker (`ImportStepQuery`) only during materialized-view maintenance (`InMViewMaintenance`), so this port refuses every next-gen FROM SELECT, as Go does outside maintenance, and `ImportStepQuery` is not ported.
findings.rust_evidence: `rust/crates/tidb-executor/src/ddl_exec.rs` (the DDL refusal), `rust/crates/tidb-planner/src/plan_builder/stmt_build.rs` and `rust/crates/tidb-session/src/dispatch.rs` (the REFRESH / PURGE / CANCEL / COMPARE and SHOW refusals), `rust/crates/tidb-session/src/import_into.rs` (the next-gen FROM SELECT refusal)

findings.finding: Statements Go executes reach the session's fallback and answer 1105 `this statement kind (...) is not supported yet`: `BINLOG '...'` (Go: OK), `REFRESH STATS` (Go: `SimpleExec`), `ALTER RANGE global PLACEMENT POLICY = ...` (Go: `executeAlterRange`), `ADMIN SHOW t NEXT_ROW_ID` (the ADMIN spelling; `SHOW TABLE t NEXT_ROW_ID` works), `SET CONFIG` (Go: `SetConfigExec`, which posts to the TiKV / PD / TiFlash HTTP config API and answers TiDB's own case with its error), and `SHOW DISTRIBUTION JOB[S]` / `CANCEL DISTRIBUTION JOB` (Go: through PD's HTTP client). For the statements Go itself refuses (`CREATE STATISTICS`, `DROP STATISTICS`, `GRANT PROXY`) Go answers 8108 `Unsupported type *ast.XxxStmt`; this port answers the 1105 fallback, although it already maps CALL to 8108. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

`ANALYZE TABLE t UPDATE HISTOGRAM ON c ...` and `DROP HISTOGRAM ON c` are refused (`this node does not run UPDATE/DROP HISTOGRAM ON`). This branch's Go parses them and `buildAnalyze` ignores `HistogramOperation`, so they run as an ordinary ANALYZE of the table with its sample-rate note. `ANALYZE ... WITH 0.5 NDVRATE` answers `NDVRATE is not a knob this node reads`, where Go's `handleAnalyzeOptions` answers `Value of analyze option NDVRATE should be positive and not larger than 0`. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

`EXPLAIN '<plan digest>'` is refused (`EXPLAIN of a plan digest is not supported yet`). Go's `buildExplain` resolves the digest through `getHintedStmtThroughPlanDigest` (statement summary) and explains the hinted statement, answering `can't find any plans for '...'` when none matches. Separately, `EXPLAIN FORMAT='cost_trace'` prints an empty `costFormula` for a Point_Get where Go prints `N/A`. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

A binding's create and update times are strings (`tidb-bindinfo` `Binding.create_time: String`), re-parsed as `TIMESTAMP(6)` when SHOW BINDINGS renders them. Go keeps `types.Time` with its own precision: a session binding is stamped `TypeTimestamp` with fsp 3 and shows `2026-11-18 13:43:06.564`, where this port shows `... 13:43:06.590000`. Global bindings agree (both read `mysql.bind_info`'s fsp 6). [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)

No Rust node hosts the AutoID service. Go's server, on a TiKV store, creates `autoid_service.New` on its status gRPC port, campaigns for `/tidb/autoid/leader` and serves `AllocAutoID` / `Rebase` for `AUTO_ID_CACHE 1` tables (`setupAutoIDService`; the `/owner_manager/auto_id_service` route in starter mode). This port only has the client (`tidb-autoid` `auto_id_client.rs`, `SinglePointAlloc`, `EtcdAutoIdLeader`); its status server registers diagnostics, the TiKV peer service and Top SQL pub-sub only. A cluster of Rust nodes has no leader to allocate those tables' IDs; it needs a Go TiDB in the cluster. (K01 recorded this under N05; N05 was closed on its HTTP routes without it.) Source-confirmed; no live TiKV run.

The next-gen keyspace services are absent. `--standby`, `--activation-timeout`, `--max-idle-seconds` and `--keyspace-activate` are parsed into `cfg.standby` / `cfg.keyspace_activate_mode` and never read, so a standby node serves at once (Go `pkg/standby`'s `LoadKeyspaceController`: `WaitForActivate`, the activation HTTP API, the idle watcher, `exitAfterKeyspaceActivate`, via `pkg/tidbmanager`). The external workload manager (`pkg/extworkload`) exists only as seam traits (`tidb-gcworker` `GcV2Manager`, the TTL job manager's boundary) with no implementation and `main.go`'s `initExternalWorkloadManager` has no counterpart. `pkg/metaservice` (per-keyspace meta service group discovery used by the TiKV driver) has no counterpart. The DXF cleanup does not send `SendRowAndSizeMeterData` (`tidb-dxf-handle` header).

Internal HTTP clients use the operating system's proxy settings. hyper-util's `client-proxy-system` is enabled through feature unification (aws-smithy), so a `reqwest` client built without `.no_proxy()` reads the macOS / Windows system proxy. Go's `util.InternalHTTPClient` uses `http.DefaultTransport` (environment variables only) or, with cluster TLS, a bare `http.Transport` with no proxy. Observed on macOS with a system proxy at 127.0.0.1:7897: `SHOW CONFIG WHERE name = 'log.level'` is empty with warning `request http://10.0.0.8:20200/config failed: 502 Bad Gateway`, where Go returns the row. `tidb-br` `conn.rs`, `import_store.rs` and the JSON report client opt out with `.no_proxy()`; `cluster_config.rs`, `metrics_reader.rs`, `tiflash_replica_manager.rs`, `cluster_http.rs` and `node_status.rs` do not. [2026-11-18 probes](structural-audit-2026-11-18.md)
